content: Before starting this medication and during its use, laboratory tests (such as liver and kidney function tests, as well as blood mineral levels) should be conducted to monitor your health. It is essential to attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose of this medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your individual health needs. Nausea, vomiting, and headaches may occur as side effects of this medication. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, voriconazole can cause severe (potentially fatal) liver disease. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are also rare. However, voriconazole commonly causes mild rashes, which are usually not serious. It may be difficult to distinguish between a mild rash and a rare rash that could indicate a severe allergic reaction. Contact your doctor if you experience any unusual symptoms. Before taking voriconazole, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other azole antifungals (such as itraconazole), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients (such as lactose) that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Voriconazole may also cause a condition that affects heart rhythm (QT prolongation). The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other drugs that can cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood can also increase this risk, especially if you are using certain medications (such as diuretics or water pills) or have conditions like severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. This medication may cause vision changes. Do not drive, operate machinery, or perform activities requiring clear vision until you are confident you can do so safely. Voriconazole may make you more sensitive to sunlight and increase your risk of skin cancer, particularly with long-term use. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, inform your doctor. You should not become pregnant while using voriconazole, as it may harm an unborn baby. Discuss reliable forms of birth control with your doctor while using this medication. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk. Due to potential risks to the infant, breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Voriconazole can slow the removal of other medications from your body, potentially affecting how they work. Similarly, other medications can affect the removal of voriconazole from your body, which may impact its effectiveness. Examples of interacting drugs include butalbital, efavirenz, mitotane, rifamycins (such as rifabutin, rifampin), ritonavir, secobarbital, and certain seizure medications (such as carbamazepine, phenobarbital). In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it for other conditions unless directed by your doctor.
